REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE BIVÅHENG PINOY DILG OPINION NO. 149 S. 2010 DEC 03 2010 HON. SHIRLYN L. BANAS-NOGRALES City Vice-Mayor General Santos City Dear Vice-Mayor Bahas-Nograles: This has reference to your earlier letter elevating to this level for our reconsideration and review the legal opinion dated 30 July 2010 rendered by DILG-Region XII. Specifically, you pose this issue for our resolution: "Whether or not herein contested IRP which was so devised by the ruling party to preempt and/or impede the presiding officer from efficiently and effectively performing her legal duties and responsibilities fall within the ambit of Republic Act Numbered Seventy—one Hundred and Sixty (RA 7160) or the Local Government Code of 1991, other existing rules of procedures, established principles of law, good customs, morals and public policies, and such other customary practices of the Sanggunian, hence valid to govern the conduct of sessions?" It may be worth to stress at the outset that your City's Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP) was already adopted by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of General Santos City by virtue of Internal Resolution No. 04, series of 2010. In this regard, please be informed that this Department has no authority to declare invalid any resolution or ordinance already enacted by the local sanggunians. Any question thereon as to the validity of the approved legislative measure should be threshed out by filing an appropriate action before the proper forum, or the concerned local sanggunian may amend the legislative measure. After a thorough examination of your arguments as well as the attachments to your letter, we find no cogent reason to enjoin the Sangguniang Panlungsod of General Santos to exercise the option of amending their approved IRP and accordingly, we affirm the legal opinion rendered by DILG-Region XII. As correctly pointed out by DILG-Region XII, IRPs may vary from one sanggunian to the other. The new sanggunian may or may not adopt the previous IRP of the former sanggunian. Section 50 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) provides that local sanggunians may make their own rules in their orderly conduct of sessions as long as such rules are not inconsistent with the 1987 Constitution, the Local Government Code and Supreme Court Decisions. The reason being that in the sources of parliamentary procedure, which are arranged in this hierarchical order: the 1987 Constitution, the Local Government Code, Judicial Decisions, Adopted Internal Rules, Parliamentary Practice, Parliamentary Authors, and Customs and Usages, IRPs come after the 1987 Constitution, the Local 20 o'

Government Code and Supreme Court Decisions, which are the higher sources. Otherwise, IRPs may be assailed and rendered invalid based on such inconsistency. Upon examination of the provisions in your IRP which you pointed out in your letter, we found no provisions therein which are inconsistent with the 1987 Constitution, the Code and Supreme Court Decisions. At this juncture, may we note that Parliamentary Practice, and Customs and Usages, from which you based your arguments, come only after the IRP so that when a parliamentary practice or a custom and usage are inconsistent with the IRP, the latter shall prevail over the former, the latter being the higher source of parliamentary procedure. If, having said the foregoing, you are still of the belief that the subject IRP was purposely devised to preempt and/or impede you from efficiently and effectively performing your legal duties and responsibilities as Presiding Officer of the Sangguniang Panlungsod, you are not precluded from filing the appropriate action before the proper forum. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, . JESU B DO UE Dir or 111 A Ls/17/rb opy Furnished: REGIONAL DIRECTOR BUAGAS B. SULAIK DILG-Region XII Koronadal City ATTY. ROCHELLE M. SERO OIC-CLGOO General Santos City
